newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends slightly down on oil demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends slightly down on oil demand.

text.p: * Central Bank sells $59 million at 26.35 pesos
The Philippine peso ended slightly down at 26.349 on Monday from 26.348 as banks chose to have dollars in view of the full deregulation of the oil industry.
"Nobody wants to get short on dollars because of oil deregulation," said a trader from a medium-sized bank.
Last Saturday, deregulation took effect and oil refiners are expected to buy more dollars with the elimination of their foreign exchange cover previously provided by the government.
But the peso traded within a narrow band from 26.345 to 26.350 as the Central Bank kept a tight rein on the market.
Traders said the Central Bank sold about $59 million at 26.35.
The day's average was at 26.349 from the previous 26.346, with volume lower at $138.05 million from $154.70 million.
Banks sold $10.7 million to one oil company today at an average of 26.349.
One oil company had informed banks it needs $60 million for this week alone compared to $75 million from the three oil firms last week, traders said. --LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
